text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Former European Commission president Jacques Delors visited Copenhagen to debate education in the 21st century at the invitation of Danish education minister Ole Vig Jensen. Delors visited local educational institutions during his visit.
--- A fresh media survey shows that while Danish firms have increased expenditure on advertising in daily newspapers and television, advertising in weekly and monthly magazines is slipping.

--- Denmark's police hope to send one or more computer hackers to prison for the first time after the biggest hacker case in Scandinavia has been before a Copenhagen court in a trial starting on Thursday. The police want firms to be more open about discussing computer security problems with them.

--- For the first time Danish shipping companies have more vessels on order at foreign yards than domestic ones. At present there are 20 ships on order at Danish yards for local shippers compared with 28 at overseas shipbuilders, with foreign-built ships often 40 percent cheaper than locally built vessels. This underlines the current crisis in Danish shipyards.
--- Denmark's fisheries sector has regained its optimism about the future after earnings increased sharply in 1995, the main problem now being the lack of young fishermen working in the sector.
